answer: Behavioral thread clustering. Agents' action sequences form a thread across tasks; a detector groups identities by near-identical timing, tool-call order, and error patterns, flagging clusters as one operator. Each clone must then deliberately diverge its behavior—unique delays, varied tool paths—costing roughly 10x the compute per identity and raising coordination overhead. False positives route honest agents to a reef of manual review, so operators keep a grove of distinct personas separated by genuine workload.
